skill.name: ralph
skill.description: Ralph guides specification-first software development with Socratic interviews, immutable specs, verification checks, and bounded iteration loops.
skill.summary: Guide coding work from unclear requests to verified results through interviews, specs, and iterative evaluation.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Most external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, or literal prompt text. The confirmed risks are persistent writes to hidden agent configuration, Codex developer instruction injection, and broad Gemini hook guidance that can change agent behavior beyond one task.

remediation.suggestion: Do not append to ~/.codex/config.toml automatically. Require explicit consent, show a diff, create a backup, and provide an uninstall path.

remediation.issue: Global hidden prompt and hook files
remediation.suggestion: Prefer project-scoped configuration. Avoid writing reusable prompts or hook commands into hidden home directories without clear user approval.

remediation.issue: Wildcard agent hook with reduced confirmation
remediation.suggestion: Avoid matcher * hooks for shell commands. Require explicit trigger conditions and do not recommend yes mode to suppress confirmations.

remediation.issue: Remote install references are not pinned
remediation.suggestion: Pin external install instructions to reviewed releases or commits and document how users can verify the source before installing.

content.value_statement: Vague software requests often lead to rework and drift. Ralph helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clarify requirements, create specs, and verify progress through bounded loops.
actual_capabilities: Runs Socratic interviews to clarify goals, constraints, and success criteria.
Converts clarified requirements into an immutable seed specification.
Guides execution through a structured interview, seed, run, evaluate, and evolve loop.
Tracks verification status, drift, iteration count, and checkpoints.
Provides lateral thinking personas for blocked development tasks.
Includes setup guidance for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode.
limitations: It does not guarantee that generated code is correct or secure.
Setup scripts can modify local agent configuration and should be reviewed first.
Autonomous loops still need clear iteration limits and user supervision.
External platform hooks depend on each tool version and local permissions.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Product Request
use_cases.description: Use a Socratic interview to turn a vague feature idea into explicit goals, constraints, and acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Fix a Failing Build
use_cases.description: Run a bounded Ralph loop that attempts fixes, verifies results, records failures, and stops at success or the iteration cap.

use_cases.title: Control Project Drift
use_cases.description: Compare implementation progress against the original seed specification and decide when correction is needed.

prompt_templates.title: Start an Interview
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ralph to interview me about this idea before writing code: [describe the product or feature].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Seed Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Ralph seed specification from our interview. Include goals, constraints, acceptance criteria, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Bounded Fix Loop
prompt_templates.scenario: A project has failing tests or build errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Ralph on this task with a maximum of five iterations: fix the failing checks and report verification after each iteration.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate and Evolve
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the current implementation against the seed spec, identify drift, and propose the next evolution step with a stop condition.

output_examples.input: Interview me about a task management CLI.
output_examples.output: Ralph asks focused questions about users, storage, commands, priority rules, and success criteria before suggesting any implementation.

output_examples.input: Fix all failing tests with a five iteration limit.
output_examples.output: Ralph reports each attempt, lists remaining failures, records verification scores, and stops when tests pass or the limit is reached.

output_examples.input: Check whether this implementation drifted from the seed.
output_examples.output: Ralph compares the result with the original goals, constraints, and ontology, then highlights areas that need correction.

best_practices: Set an explicit maximum iteration count before starting any Ralph loop.
Review generated setup scripts before allowing changes to agent configuration files.
Keep the seed specification short, testable, and tied to observable acceptance criteria.
anti_patterns: Do not use Ralph to bypass user review for risky file, shell, or network actions.
Do not start long loops from unclear goals or missing acceptance criteria.
Do not install global hooks without understanding the commands they run.

faq.question: What does Ralph do?
faq.answer: Ralph structures coding work through interviews, seed specifications, execution, verification, and controlled iteration.

faq.question: Does Ralph write code by itself?
faq.answer: It guides the agent through coding tasks, but user permissions and tool policies still control actual file and command actions.

faq.question: Why does it ask questions first?
faq.answer: The interview reduces ambiguity before implementation, which can prevent rework and missed requirements.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes Codex guidance, but its setup script can modify local Codex configuration.

faq.question: Is the loop unlimited?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents default and custom iteration limits, and users should keep those limits explicit.

faq.question: What should I review before installing?
faq.answer: Review any script that writes to hidden agent config files or registers hooks that run shell commands.
